title: monday.com MCP Server
summary: Run monday.com's official MCP server locally in read-only mode so your agent can inspect boards and items without changing anything.
description: monday.com publishes an MCP server as the npm package @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp. It gives an agent tools to read board schemas, fetch items, and, when allowed, create items, post updates and change column values.

This setup starts it through npx with the documented --read-only flag, so write tools are left out. You supply a personal API token through the MONDAY_TOKEN variable. Drop the flag later if you want the agent to edit boards.
useWhen: Look up what is on the product roadmap board before planning work
Check the status column of a bug item
List which items are in a group and who owns them
Read a board's columns before writing an integration against it

mcp.name: monday
access: Reads boards, items, columns and users that your token can see
Read-only while the --read-only flag stays in the args

example.prompt: Which items on the Sprint Board are stuck and who owns them?
example.result: 2 items have status Stuck: "Webhook retries" (owner Priya) and "SSO redirect loop" (owner Marcus). Both were last updated 4 days ago.

faq.question: Where do I find the token?
faq.answer: In monday.com, open your profile menu, then Developers, then My access tokens. Store it in your shell environment as MONDAY_TOKEN.

faq.question: How do I allow edits?
faq.answer: Remove --read-only from the args. The agent then gets tools to create items, post updates and change column values.

faq.question: Is there a hosted option?
faq.answer: Yes, the repository also lists a hosted URL, https://mcp.monday.com/mcp. This setup uses the local package because it has a documented read-only switch.

access: monday.com boards your token can see, read-only by default here
